# The initial idea was to push back and have Couriers register themselves separately with the municipality, Bolt would send Couriers monthly reports of confirmations of orders from LEZ restaurant / LEZ client that Couriers would then submit to the municipality and municipality would deduct those from the final bill for entering LEZ.



The municipality did not agree to this proposal and we faced two options:

# Either we share Courier phone number, Order (delivered to/from LEZ) pick-up and drop off date and time; or
# We don’t get any exception from municipality and pay fees out of our pockets.



[~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] highlighted the risks of sharing the personal data initially requested by the municipality (prior fines to competitors, extensive data-sharing → the municipality wanted delivery address, start of the order address, other relevant info)

* We agreed to share the minimum necessary: Courier phone number, Order (delivered to/from LEZ) pick-up and drop off date and time as an alternative to license plates in RH → municipality agreed to the minimized data



Our legal representative at the municipality discussed the issue with city’s DPO:

* DPO said platforms would have to amend their couriers registration rules and require them to register in “Parking in Kaunas” + amend their PNs
* DPO said they didn’t find information on what legal basis platforms should rely on, recommended consent checkbox



*Privacy response:*

* Not to push back on PN amendments - transparency is our requirement under GDPR
* Rely on legitimate interest



*Next steps:*

* DPIA
* LIA
* Drafting a DSA with municipality
* Update local PN
* Solve comms to Drivers / Couriers regarding update in data sharing

analysis was done by looking at data from September/2024.

I’ve pulled every in-app order that didn’t have preauth. main metric will be from the columns:

* *max_risk_cost*: the assumption is that if an order had an initial failed payment, the user could run into the same error in the preauth that could cause the order not to be created. _max_risk_cost_ tracks the worst possible scenario where every single order that matches this criteria ends up not being created. loss to us is the order GMV vs Rides 8% profitability.
* *min_savings_same_price*: this column represents our main saving. if the order’s final price remains equal to or smaller than the amount we have authorized and is currently uncovered, then the payment won’t fail anymore.

*max_risk_cost* isn’t realistic. users should be able to change payment methods or top-up their cards to still create orders.

on the other end, *min_savings_same_price* is a guaranteed win.

therefore, if (*min_savings_same_price* - *max_risk_cost*) is positive, the outcome should be positive for Bolt.

the tab *_simplified numbers on the country level_* on the following sheet has country numbers: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18v_OnyknnNbaIIj3dDIbn18zSd5F8h5328-QX5bvICk/edit?gid=0#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18v_OnyknnNbaIIj3dDIbn18zSd5F8h5328-QX5bvICk/edit?gid=0#gid=0|smart-link]

for some countries, if we start doing preauth for literally every single in-app order, the outcome should be positive. TH for example, has a *max_risk_cost* of 5.4k euros and *min_savings_same_price* of 10.1k euros. we would reduce 10.1k euros in failed payments risking at max 5.4k euros of net good GMV.

Thank you for your patience. So, the case described is: 

A scooter user has an accident with a bike and:

* The user gets minor injuries
* The third-party bike is damaged
* The user claims the reason for the incident is faulty breaks

The expectations are that: 

* The user will not be covered by insurance because injuries are minor,  *but* 
* The third party would be covered, as the reason for the accident *is not* the user’s breach of T&Cs (tandem riding, drunk riding, etc).

engineering team has proposed the following recommendations:

During the pre-check process, the Data Migration (DM) tool utilizes the GTID specified in the configuration file for its verification. It's important to note that these GTIDs may not encompass all purged GTIDs, especially since previous tasks have been running for some time and some binlogs may have been purged since the start.

In this situation, it is essential to recover from the existing task and use the GTID from the previous checkpoint.

To obtain the GTID from the checkpoint, please execute the following SQL query on the downstream system, and subsequently update the task configuration accordingly:

{noformat}SELECT * FROM dm_meta.<task-name>_syncer_checkpoint WHERE is_global=1;{noformat}

Alternatively, you may choose to bypass this pre-check item by setting the {{ignore-checking-items}} parameter to include "meta_position." Additionally, please ensure that the binlogs required by DM have not been purged, as this could result in the same error being reported again.

While doing research, these were some of the trends that were mentioned that could also easily apply to the Bolt Training context: 

*Blended learning* 

This concept combines classroom learning with practical components to reinforce learned theory concepts/information. Along with this concept, skills-based learning was also seen taking an upward trend, with soft skills taking the main priority/interest. 

_How we can implement_ 

* Add opportunities to practice in the form of more real-life scenarios, simulations, offline projects and case studies
* Consider creating live session facilitation guides for OS Trainers to use when having classroom sessions with new joiners 

*Automating Administrative tasks* 

AI is seeming all the buzz these days and one such use case is to automate administrative tasks that are repetitive to spend more time focused on results-bearing tasks. 

_How we can implement_ 

* Improve/elevate templates for curriculum that can be copied and reused
* Use AI for basic curriculum plans then personalising for the Bolt user context
* Research automating tasks that are possible with TLMS 
* Look into ways to automate grading, feedback, reporting 

*Microlearning*

With high backlogs, changing products and general information fatigue, it can be difficult for agents to sit down and focus on full-length training on a repetitive cycle. It is for this reason that microlearning is seeing an upward trend in training. It's the perfect solution to get training time in with a lower time implication. 

These can also be used for the purposes of refresher or retraining courses on individual CS processes.

_How we can implement_ 

* Create a quarterly-based schedule where agents go through topics to refresh their understanding of processes they are using every day to support customers 

*Courses from/with Subject Matter Experts*

As it stands today, training is created and designed by the TPM and TD. Without knowing, there may be times when some information or logic may fall through the cracks. This is what makes courses from subject matter experts so appealing. 

Based on the idea of platforms such as [+Masterclass+|https://www.masterclass.com/], these types of courses/podcasts/videos appeal to users because the information is coming from someone who has a good amount of knowledge on the topic. This also comes with sharing some best practices and some ‘hidden’ information one might only have access to when they use CS tools frequently. 

_How we can implement_ 

* Add snippets of recorded video of workflows from an agent in courses 
* Add pro-tips from agents / Work Senior Support agents into the training materials in the form of quotes, best practices, etc.  

Other concepts that were great but are a bit challenging to implement: 

* +Alternate ways to assess agents+ understanding pf concepts - not all KPIs that we track will always be perfect for every training we roll out. In this case, we may need to use different ways to assess agents fairly 
* VR/XR to have agents simulate the customer experience or journey so that they can ‘put themselves in the customers shoes’ 
* Neuroeducation-based learning paths for different agents and their learning needs - this would also speak to DEI 

*Other idea - not from training* 

* In a bid to support getting 100% completion rates, it could be helpful to break course rollout into cohorts and groups so Trainers have a better focus on agent progress 
** In this case say we have 2 courses running - group A would complete it in week 1 - 2 while group B would complete it in week 3 - 4 
* Data correction prompt - automation or message to prompt Trainers/TL’s to update their team lists so we know we have enrolled the correct agents who are also not on longer leaves

[~accountid:712020:b2a2738f-c1f1-447c-9b72-29851b5fed3e] For Web;


* Yes, the collection of data via Rudderstack on the web is indeed subject to the Cookie Banner's compliance framework. Users must explicitly give their consent to enable such data collection, and without this consent, the pipeline would not be activated.
* This aligns with GDPR and other privacy regulations, ensuring that any data collected complies with user preferences.

For App;


* if Appsflyer is placed as an optional tool within the DMA/ePD consent solution, its trackers would only activate if the user consents to it. In this setup, Appsflyer's activities, including data processing and transfers, would indeed require user consent in order to comply with relevant privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, etc.).
* Without this consent, any Appsflyer-based data collection would not proceed, ensuring transparency and compliance.

Overall view;


* AEM aggregates data without user-specific identifiers, ensuring no Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is shared. The use of anonymized data aligns with industry standards for privacy-preserving ad measurement.
* The collection of IP and IDFV is standard practice for attribution, and this data is processed through tools (e.g., Rudderstack, Appsflyer) with robust security measures.
* By implementing AEM, we can optimize iOS campaigns more effectively, especially given the limitations of Apple’s ATT framework. Without AEM, we lose valuable data from non-consenting users, which impacts campaign efficiency and ROI.Example: AEM allows us to attribute installs and in-app events for both consenting and non-consenting users, giving us a more complete dataset to improve targeting and spend allocation.

_Exmo. Senhor Dr. Luís Sommer Ribeiro, boa tarde,_

_Agradecemos e acusamos a receção do e-mail infra, o qual mereceu a nossa melhor atenção._

_Em primeiro lugar, lamentamos saber que a atividade da Bolt Market esteja a provocar incómodo junto dos moradores do edifício, o que vai integralmente contra o que é pretendido e desejado pela Bolt Market._

_A verdade é que a Bolt Market exerce a sua atividade no aludido local desde 2021 e desde então tem vindo a adotar mecanismos concludentes com as regras de boa vizinhança e civismo, atuando com boa-fé, procurando encontrar as melhores soluções que beneficiem todas as partes envolvidas e que não prejudiquem de forma séria a atividade desenvolvida pela Bolt Market no referido local._

_No sentido de prestar esclarecimentos e facultar potenciais soluções para algumas das situações abordadas relativamente aos pontos levantados no seu e-mail, damos nota do seguinte:_

# *_Concentração de Estafetas e Uso Indevido do Espaço Público_*

_Compreendemos o incómodo resultante da aglomeração de estafetas_{color:#0747a6} {color}_sentida em frente ao edifício em causa. No entanto, cumpre-nos esclarecer que os estafetas não são trabalhadores da Bolt Market, pelo que a Bolt Market não detém qualquer controlo/poder de direção sobre os mesmos nem pode determinar que estes cumpram quaisquer regras específicas que pretendam que sejam implementadas para mitigar o problema apresentado. Não obstante, e como prova de boa-fé, cuidado e zelo com que pauta a sua atividade, a Bolt Market já tinha recomendado aos estafetas em causa para que ficassem a aguardar pelo seu pedido num local afastado da entrada do prédio. Apesar de não controlar as ações/omissões dos estafetas e como forma de mitigar os constrangimentos que se têm vindo a sentir junto dos moradores, a Bolt compromete-se a transmitir as preocupações do condomínio, reforçando novamente junto dos estafetas tal recomendação._

_Por outro lado, e mais concretamente relativamente ao “consumo de substâncias ilícitas“ por parte dos estafetas, a Bolt Market não só não tem qualquer conhecimento de que tal se esteja a verificar, como é totalmente alheia a tais ocorrências, nem as mesmas são da sua responsabilidade, porquanto, reitera-se, os estafetas não são trabalhadores da Bolt Market._

# *_Entregas e Actividades Fora de Horário Regulamentado_*

_A Bolt é uma sociedade comercial que tem vindo a cumprir e pretende continuar a cumprir com todas as disposições legais que lhe sejam aplicáveis.  No entanto, novamente numa lógica de boa-fé, a Bolt Market irá tentar reduzir ao máximo o eventual ruído que resulte das entregas com os fornecedores. Para além deste esforço, e já no que diz respeito à entrega de mercadorias pelo fornecedores, a Bolt Market irá solicitar aos fornecedores que vêm entregar mercadorias logo pela manhã que desliguem os seus veículos aquando das entregas para reduzir o ruído na via pública. Contudo, uma vez mais, dado que os aludidos fornecedores não são trabalhadores da Bolt Market, tal poderá não surtir o efeito pretendido e a recomendação poderá não ser acatada._

# *Ruído Excessivo e Contínuo*

_A Bolt Market dedica a sua atividade comercial ao funcionamento de um mercado/mercearia online de produtos alimentares, sendo certo que o estabelecimento comercial em causa gere os pedidos de produtos que são solicitados pelos utilizadores da plataforma, organiza-os, entrega aos estafetas que vêm recolhê-los ao estabelecimento, e também aceita entregas de mercadorias de fornecedores. Em suma, a atividade que produz um ruído excessivo e contínuo diz respeito apenas e tão-só ao processo de entrega e recolha de produtos alimentares. A Bolt Market acredita que esta concreta atividade não produz o mesmo ruído que seja suscetível de provocar a diminuição da qualidade de vida dos moradores, quando comparando com outro tipo de atividades comerciais que se registam na cidade de Lisboa._

_Acresce que, a Bolt Market, por ser, como se disse, um mercado/mercearia online de produtos alimentares, necessita encarecidamente de utilizar sistemas de ar condicionado e que estes estejam em pleno funcionamento para conseguir garantir as normas de Qualidade e Segurança Alimentar. Neste sentido, é manifestamente impossível retirar os sistemas de ar condicionado por estes serem imprescindíveis não só para o pleno funcionamento da atividade comercial da Bolt Market, mas também para que a Bolt Market cumpra com todas as normas de higiene alimentar e de saúde relativamente às quais está legalmente obrigada. No entanto, damos nota de que relativamente a este tema,_ {color:#0747a6}_será em breve (ou eventualmente já terá sido) contactado_{color}_, na qualidade de advogado mandatado pelo condomínio porquanto o proprietário do local no qual a Bolt Market exerce a sua atividade contratou um técnico de sistemas de ar condicionado para verificar se existe alguma possibilidade de reduzir o ruído produzido pelos mesmos._

_Conforme pode constatar, a Bolt Market encontra-se comprometida a zelar pelo bem-estar dos moradores em causa, pretendendo em total boa-fé implementar todas as soluções que permitam mitigar quaisquer danos decorrentes da sua atividade, em adequada proporção com a necessidade de manter a sua atividade comercial em pleno funcionamento, dentro dos moldes expectáveis e aceitáveis._

_A Bolt Market mantém-se igualmente disponível para dialogar, caso considere necessário._

_Com os melhores cumprimentos,_

** However, we can only rely on this where ‘necessity’ and ‘balancing exercise’ limbs are also fulfilled.
* Therefore, data requested must be proportionate / necessary, and the rights and interests of the user whose data we are disclosing here must not outweigh the rights / interests of the requesting data subject.

[~accountid:5e4cfe3b393ea90c94b40eb0] I confirm the following: 

From a legal perspective, the reclassification risk is low in Nigeria following two recent judgments confirming that drivers are independent contractors. 

Acceptance Rate Blocking: ARB is mechanism used to manage driver performance by blocking drivers whose acceptance rate falls below a certain threshold. The acceptance rate is calculated based on the percentage of orders accepted from the past 100 requests. If a driver's acceptance rate falls below the city-specific threshold, they may be blocked for varying durations. ARB is the riskiest feature for Bolt from a reclassification perspective because it amounts to Bolt exercising control over the drivers _Bolt is reducing the ability to access work if the driver does not accept work._

The new proposed feature DQO is a less risky feature to ARB. 

Driver Queue Optimiser: The feature uses an availability model to predict rejections and cancellations for orders, removing drivers with low predicted finish rates from the matching list to improve user experience and marketplace efficiency. The model can reorder drivers based on the probability of rejection or cancellation, applying a modifier to the ETA of each driver to prioritize those with higher success rates. It is particularly useful in markets with high driver rejections and cancellations. *That said*  DQO Can “very easily” be used to make arguments that drivers are subordinate to Bolt and Bolt is controlling drivers like employees: Bolt is carrying out ‘ongoing performance assessments’ to determine who is best suited for work.

*From a legal perspective, DQO has the green light to be tested in Nigeria.* 

The main factor would be from an operational perspective taking into account driver behaviour and the prevailing circumstance in Nigeria (e.g. high ETAs because of traffic).

In confirm in my conversation with [~accountid:712020:7250d115-7c52-46bf-8d9f-1a48a1d58b25] that he is comfortable to test out the DQO feature and monitor the driver engagement following successful testing of the blast dispatch feature.

Dear Fatima,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 8 November 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including passengers). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore attach copies of your personal data to which you are entitled.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

I just yesterday shared with [~accountid:61236e891827d100682bc017]  legal analysis from [~accountid:712020:a9ca1df5-fe05-4efc-9bb7-f89fd653ec94] regarding 1P sales in PL. Part of it covered also controversial products (including non-alcoholic beer). You can find the overview about PL [HERE |https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1HDc8ED6twbRpxtMXXnVvGFWLUn9BsOhX/edit?gid=1849116909#gid=1849116909]under the tab “Details” row 32 H. As far as I know Janis should have added relevant information also into the new version of moderation guidelines. 

Just in case copying the answer from the table also here:

*_Alcohol_*_. The retailers must obtain a relevant licence for selling alcohol products. The matter of alcohol online sale is complex and subject to various legal doubts and subject to verdicts of administrative courts. The regulations do not state clearly whether such sale is possible however a verdict of Supreme Administrative Court indirectly allowing such sale was issued. At the same time in publicly available source it is possible to find govermnetal articles in which it is stated online alcohol sale is forbidden._ +_The advertisement of alcoholic beverages is strictly forbidden, excluding beer. Beer may be advertised, however such advertisement may not be directed to person under the age of 18, it cannot be published via media or sports events held for minors, it may not encourage to excessive consumption of beer, it cannot associate drinkin beer with driving car or other hazardous activities. Public ads of beer may be held on small boards within areas where beer is sold. The ads via TV, radio, cinema or theather shall not be visale between 6 AM and 8 PM. Ads must contain clear and visiable information concerning harmful influence of alcohol as well as prohibition of selling alcohol to minors. Such information cover at least 20% of ad area._+ 

*_Non-alcoholic beer/similar._* _Non-alcoholic beer/cider/wine have no special status in Poland and are essentially considered soft drinks. However according to legal regulations concerning beer, it is forbidden to promote products or services name, trademark, graphics or packaging of which is simmiliar or same to alcohol-product. Thus_ +_it is recommendable to promote non-alhocolic beer/similiar on the same basis as alcohol products._+

I have reviewed DAAO specification and done a ride test with different acceleration currents.

Comparison table of both motors:

||*Parameter*||*DAAO 500W*||*Jinshun 350W*||
|Rated voltage|48V|36V|
|Rated power|*500W*|350W|
|Rated current|*12± 0.5A/7.5N*m*|10.2± 0.5A/5.9 N*m|
|Max torque|25A≥30Nm|15A≥22Nm|
|Enamelled wire specification|*0.51 - QZ-2-155*|0.51 - QZ-1-130L|
|Coil winding|*9 strands*
11 turns|8 strands
12 turns|
|Cross sectional area of winding|0.2mm2 x 9 = *1.8mm2*|0.2mm2 x 8 = 1.6mm2|
|IP rating|IP54|*IPX7*|

DAAO 500W is electrically more suitable for Dragon than Jinshun 350W motor. 

*DAAO advantages:* 

# *Larger copper cross sectional area.* 1.8mm2 for DAAO vs 1.6mm2 for Jinshun. Larger area means less heat generated in the coil. 
# *Higher grade coil insulation.* DAAO is using insulation Grade 2 with working temperature of 155°C. Whereas Jinshun is using Grade 1 with working temperature of 130°C. This means that DAAO insulation can withstand higher temperatures.

Only concern i have with DAAO motor is the ingress protection rating IP54. 

I asked DAAO if they can make the motor more waterproof and their answer was that they have to modify the mold of the oil seal from 5mm to 7mm. 
We compared the seals from both motors with [~accountid:5e4658b55a495e0c91a7a011] and found that the seal used on Jinshun motor can also be used on DAAO. Another thing we discovered is that Jinshun motor has an additional gasket on the side shield. Adding pictures for reference.

!image (10).png|width=1135,height=851,alt="image (10).png"!

Picture 1. Oil seals; DAAO on the left, Jinshun on the right

!image (11).png|width=479,height=290,alt="image (11).png"!

Picture 2. Side shield gasket and groove

h1. Ride test

Ride tests were done on flat ground, uphill and downhill. 

On flat ground the scooter maintained top speed throughout the ride. No abnormalities were detected. 

Riding uphill, DAAO motor has a slight advantage at 25A acceleration current. Picture 3 shows that uphill speed was slightly higher with DAAO motor. Battery voltage was 53V for both tests, acceleration current was set to 25A and speed limit to 25 km/h. 
Using lower acceleration currents showed that both motors were equal in speed and current consumption.

!image-20241205-204522.png|width=798,height=578,alt="image-20241205-204522.png"!

Picture 3. 25A acceleration current, speed limit 25 km/h

h1. Conclusion

DAAO 500W motor would be a suitable alternative for Dragon scooters if DAAO can improve their ingress protection rating.

For example, let's use the 350W power limiter logic. We allow the motor to run at 25A for 3 minutes, then we lower the acceleration current to 18A and let it run for 12 more minutes. After that time we lower the current to 7A. Our top speed is 25kmh.

Personally I think that, if Jinshun is willing to make a new motor, then we need to write a specification first. I could start doing the specification on Monday.

Dear Mikhel,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 8 November 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including drivers). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore attach copies of your personal data to which you are entitled.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/et-ee/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/et-ee/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

* in conditional campaigns we are not never triggering monitoring for  {{event failed}} , for example if no periodEnrollmentId found or we just return without any monitoring
* we had {{next_period_notification_cutoff_seconds}}  config for driver campaign which we dint require yet for conditional campaigns as personal periods dint exist yet

so the question for us is: {{do we really want to have event monitoring for failures in conditional campaigns or not}}
we have not been doing it for other issues related to conditional campaigns so doesnt seem like we really need it. just logger have sufficed so far.if we dont want event monitoring then really dont see the need for this endpoint.

Please find here below (1) a succinct summary of the facts provided by Kista; (2) a legal analysis of whether mediation should have been undertaken by the rider before going to court; (3) suggested next steps. 



# *Summary of Facts*

+Timeline+: from the data that can be evidenced, the rider did not leave sufficient time to reach the bus station (data includes time of order, time of arrival of the diver, ETA of the trip, and time of the departure of the bus).

+Material evidence+: we have a message from the driver warning Bolt of the problematic encounter with this rider, and the exchange between Bolt’s customer service and the rider to assist in his complaint.



# *Obligation of Mediation*

+Bolt’s Passenger T&Cs+

* Step 1 = file a claim to Bolt (on the app or by email: [+paris@bolt.eu+|mailto:paris@bolt.eu]) 
* Step 2 = without any settlement or satisfactory outcome through a claim to Bolt, the Passager should apply to a claim in mediation : Association Nationale des Médiateurs (ANM)
* Step 3 (alternative) = Passager can file a claim through the mediation service of the European Commission

+Code de la consommation, Article L612-4+: La clause contractuelle ne peut obliger à recourir obligatoirement à une médiation préalable

[https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000032224798|https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000032224798|smart-link] 

+Code de procédure civil, Article 131-1:+ Ordonnance par le juge d’une médiation

[https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/id/LEGISCTA000030360397|https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/id/LEGISCTA000030360397|smart-link] - Après avoir recueilli l’accord des parties, le juge peut ordonner une médiation.

+Code de procédure civil, Article 750-1+: Demande irrecevable si aucune tentative de médiation à été engagé

[https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000039501708/|https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000039501708/|smart-link] - Juge peut prononcer d'office la demande en justice irrecevable, si celle ci-n'est pas précédée d'une tentative de conciliation, tentative de médiation ou tentative de procédure participative pour des paiements de somme n’excédant pas 5000 EUR.

*Conclusion:* Le non-respect d’une clause de médiation est une question de recevabilité et non de compétence (confirmé dans un arrêt de la Cour de Cassation rendu le 1er février 2023). 



# *Suggested Next Steps*

La contestation de la convocation doit être formulée sur le fondement du défaut de tentative de médiation en vertu de l’article 650-1 du Code de Procédure Civile.

En première instance, dès la réception de la convocation, Bolt peut demander un report de l'audience en précisant que le demandeur n'a pas tenté de médiation préalable. Cette demande devra être adressée par lettre recommandée avec accusé de réception au tribunal. 

En deuxième instance, Bolt peut soulever l’irrecevabilité de la demande dans un délai de 15 jours avant l’audience.

Hi [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3], I'm adding to the part about sharing interviews with trainees. How BrightHire Works with GDPR:

*Data Subject Consent:* we need to obtain consent from candidates (data subjects) before their interview recordings are shared, especially for training purposes. BrightHire allows companies to manage this by ensuring that explicit consent is obtained during and before the interview process or as part of the candidate's agreement.

*Data Minimization:* BrightHire encourages practices that support data minimization, meaning only the necessary interview data is shared for training purposes. This can include anonymizing or redacting personal data where feasible, and limiting access to sensitive information.

*Access Control:* Only authorized users (e.g., interviewer trainees, managers, or trainers) can access the shared interview recordings, ensuring that only the people who need the training material can view the content. Permissions and roles are strictly controlled.

*Data Retention and Deletion:* BrightHire allows the setting up of retention policies and ensures interview recordings are deleted when they are no longer needed or at the candidate's request.

*Audit and Transparency:* BrightHire tracks and logs all actions related to interview recordings (e.g., sharing, access, and viewing), providing transparency and accountability. 

*Data Transfer and Security:* BrightHire ensures that interview data is transferred and stored securely with encryption, both in transit and at rest. This safeguards data against unauthorized access.

This is a case study document [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5641109603/2024-12-05+Case+Study+Improve+the+User-based+strategy+for+Live+Tracing|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5641109603/2024-12-05+Case+Study+Improve+the+User-based+strategy+for+Live+Tracing|smart-link] 

Main thoughts: 

* It is already possible to perform the “cross-team user-based Live Tracing“. Once you start tracing in one service, Tempo receives traces from all the downstream services as well. 
* It is already possible to configure services from other teams. It requires RnA flow for live and just works for prelive
* I don’t see a need to handle user_id between services. If we speak debug case, developers should know the entry point services for the request. This is enough to track the whole request path. Nothing is needed in addition

*The most important:*

Nobody will use Live Tracing with the current interaction design. It’s too cumbersome. I insist on the refactoring of the general approach UI/UX of Live Tracing. These are my ideas in the case study above. It seems this ticket is related [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-1991|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-1991|smart-link]. Main ideas are:

* Deprecate the raw json configuration approach
* Dedicated configuration pages per sampling strategy: user-based and path-based
* Convenient UI on these pages, this means NO raw json configs. Possibility to configure several services at once
* It must be possible to enable traces only for the time period. This is security and general stability improvement.

so… rounding :smiling_face_with_tear: 

* invoice row has sum of all trips made in period
* each individual row has 21% VAT
* if we just sum values {{sum}}, {{vat_sum}} , {{sum_with_vat}} from individual orders we'll get [3033.56 net, 636.83 vat, 3670.39 gross]
* however as you can see 3033.56 * 1.21 = 3670.61 which is not equal to what we have to invoice (3670.39)
* so that's why we are recalculating {{sum}} and {{vat_sum}} on invoice row level based on {{sum_with_vat}} and {{vat_percentage}} so we have valid numbers on the invoice

in human terms it means that for the CSV {{sum, vat_sum , sum_with_vat}} are taken from the ride invoices while for the invoice basically the calculation is done in reverse: we take the gross sum from the CSV and recalculate the net sum and vat_sum based on the gross. sounds about correct [~accountid:609f85c48cbda700686da854]? :smiling_face_with_tear: 

To be honest I have no ideas how to make it better either but our product team is looking into all rounding related issues and trying to find a solution so these kinds of discrepancies would disappear.

To start a service you need to set up multiple pieces of dependencies. There are pieces which already have easy-to-use per-service commands, there are pieces which have some granularity, but are less obvious to map to service, and there is still some global setup. I propose to:

# Take commands like {{yarn setup:create-database <path>}} and allow to specify {{service-id}} instead of the current parameters
# Take previous commands and existing per-service commands and put them together into a single command like {{yarn start:auto <service-id>}} 
# Keep the rest of the global dependencies under {{yarn setup}}

----

Currently, to start a service, you need to:

# Run {{yarn setup:docker}}, which includes
## {{yarn install}} – we have global install without an option to split it yet
## {{yarn setup:docker-start}} – stars up Colima, or makes sure it’s started
## {{yarn setup:docker-login}} – makes sure you have access to Artifactory/JFrog
## {{yarn setup:docker-pull}} – pulls ALL images
## {{yarn setup:docker-reset}} – does more, not only Docker-related stuff 😄 
### {{yarn setup:hosts}} – makes sure you have all needed entries in {{/etc/hosts}} for Docker to work locally
### {{yarn setup:docker-up}} – starts ALL Docker containers
### {{yarn setup:wait-and-create-databases}} – runs a script with DB setup for ALL DB schemas which includes multiple steps
#### waits for ALL DB containers to start (3 containers, 1 per engine)
#### drops ALL DB schemas
#### creates ALL DB schemas from {{.sql}} files
# Run {{yarn dependencies:minimal <service-id>}} – save output as {{<services>}} ({{yarn dependencies:minimal}} works with space-separated services, everything else works with comma-separate services, {{<services>}} are comma-separated from here on)
# Run {{yarn setup:localstack <services>}} – create missing SNS/SQS resources
# Run {{yarn clean:db <taxify_schema_name>}} – insert seed data into the DB, this is highly contextual, as some of the services can’t start without this data (like {{taxify_config_store}}, or {{taxify_admin_user}}), while for others it’s just something handy for local testing, also need to know DB schema names at this point for all services
# Run {{yarn compile:service <services>}}
# Run {{yarn start <services>}}

This can be split into “environment setup” which usually do once per development session, “service setup” which is getting all of the dependencies up and running, and “service startup” - actually running the service.

h3. Environment setup

This you usually do once per development session and that’s it. This is just making sure you have all of the basics up-to-date and running. One global command is more than enough for it.

In its current form, {{yarn setup:docker}} largely fulfills this function, but there are two things that don’t fully belong here:

# Docker container sync & startup – ideally, each service would have their own set of Docker dependencies which it needs. Some containers are specific to a very narrow set of services, yet currently we set up absolutely ALL of them ALL of the time. This is a subject for a separate discussion, and I would leave it for its own ticket. For now let’s keep Docker in the “environment setup”, hoping that it will be moving to “service setup” at some point.
# DB setup – we don’t need to set up ALL DBs, this is actually pretty time consuming and often wasteful. DB setup should move to “service setup”.

Note that there’s also {{yarn setup}} which runs an extra {{yarn setup:completions}}. I would prefer using {{yarn setup}} as the main setup method, but a lot of people are used to {{yarn setup:docker}}, just because it’s been abused as the “setup of everything”. 

h3. Service setup

These are the steps which you need to run to set up specific service’s dependencies. Ideally, anything that we can do per-service should go here. You usually do it once per development, but it’s more likely that you’ll need to redo it – you want to recreate the schema after you’ve updated it, or you want to provision new queues for your new publisher, etc. In this case, a command to do a full service setup for a single service or a list of services would be really useful to blackbox the complexity. But at the same time it would be great to have access to specific setup steps (still per-service) in case any of them has to be rerun separately, just because it will allow to iterate faster than having to reset the full setup, and because it might not be desirable to reset other things.

For the full service setup, I propose to introduce {{yarn setup:service <service-id> [<other-service-id]}} command. It should automatically include services from minimal dependencies and all of their dependent resources as well.

Partial reset can be available via separate commands like {{yarn setup:create-databases <service-id>}} (but they should be service ID based!) or as an option on the main command, for example {{yarn setup:service <service-id> --only=db}}.

h3. Service startup

This is literally just starting the service. This includes two steps – compiling and running. This is expected to be run frequently throughout development.

Here, we already have {{yarn compile:service <services>}} and {{yarn start <services>}} that take care of everything. There’s a way to recompile and restart the service automatically as well using {{nodemon}}, although it’s not exposed via a simple command: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4367909971/How+to+automatically+restart+a+service+after+a+code+change|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4367909971/How+to+automatically+restart+a+service+after+a+code+change|smart-link] We don’t currently have a way to compile+run the service quickly, perhaps we could add {{yarn start:with-compile <service-id>}}, to match {{yarn ctest:with-compile}} which seems to be getting traction.

The important part is to connect “service startup” to other types of startup.

* We can offer {{yarn start:with-setup <service-id>}} to run {{yarn setup:service <service-id>}} and then {{yarn start:with-compile <services>}} for all resulting services. 
* We can offer {{yarn quickstart <service-id>}} (or maybe {{yarn start:quick <service-id>}} or some other version of {{yarn start:<smth>}} or even {{yarn start:with-<smth>}} to follow the convention) to run {{yarn setup}} followed by {{yarn start:with-setup <service-id>}}

----

To recap, this would be the minimal list of things to do with our current setup:

# Make {{yarn setup:create-databases}} work with {{<service-id>}}
# Make {{yarn clean:db}} work with {{<service-id>}}
# Implement {{yarn setup:service <service-id> [<other-service-id>]}}, which would:
## Run {{yarn dependencies:minimal <service-id>}} producing a list of {{<services>}}
## {{Run yarn setup:localstack <services>}}
## Run {{yarn setup:create-databases <services>}}
## Run {{yarn clean:db <services>}}
# Implement {{yarn start:with-setup <service-id>}}, which would:
## Run {{yarn setup:service <service-id>}} producing a list of {{<services>}}
## Run {{yarn start:with-compile <services>}} (or {{yarn compile:services <services> && yarn start <services>}})
# Implement {{yarn quickstart <service-id>}}, which would:
## Run {{yarn setup}}
## Run {{yarn start:with-setup <service-id>}}

The following rather count as additional improvements:

# Implement {{yarn start:with-compile <service-id>}}
# Make service setup commands more uniform, like {{yarn setup:service:db}} or {{yarn setup:service --only=db}}

Thanks [~accountid:712020:2449585e-020b-4bbc-ac29-8780f94f6823] - I have taken a look at the below and have included some initial {color:#4c9aff}*thoughts*{color} / {color:#ff5630}*questions*{color}. In short:

* Gender data is certainly something we can collect, but we need to be careful on how we do so. IMO, we should avoid using AI technology to scan a user’s photo / ID to determine their gender, but should instead either: (a) leverage the existing tools we have to extract information about a user’s gender where this is included in their ID; and, failing that (b) resort to manual review. Let us know if this is an approach that could be feasible.
* We would need to make some privacy notice updates if we took this approach.
* Ideally, we should store this data on Admin rather than in separate files / spreadsheets / etc.

Further details are below. I appreciate there is a fair bit of info here, so {color:#4c9aff}*I suggest we hop on a call next week*{color} to make sure we are aligned - let me know when works for you. (cc. [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] - let me know if any of this goes against what has previously been advised and I can adapt it)

*Preferred method for verifying a rider's gender*

Ideally, we would prefer to {color:#4c9aff}*avoid using AI technology to scan a user’s face*{color} to determine their gender - this triggers a few requirements under data protection law with regards to biometric processing that would likely create headaches for us in the long term.
Given that Bolt already has tools in place to scan ID documents and extract certain datapoints as part of the verification process, {color:#4c9aff}*our preferred approach from a Privacy POV would be to*{color} {color:#4c9aff}*try and leverage these tools to extract information about a user’s gender* {color}{color:#4c9aff}*_where this is included in their ID_*{color} (i.e., a user’s ID document specifies whether they are male or female). This is preferable because it would help us to circumvent any possible issues with inaccuracy, and would also mean we are not being overly invasive with the data we are collecting. To make this work, I suppose we would need to do an assessment of which jurisdictions have IDs that specify gender, and then make sure that we are specifying that users should provide this as part of the verification process - {color:#ff5630}*is this something you think would be feasible?* {color}We would need to discuss with the Ops / ID teams to check whether this would work.
Where gender is not specified in a user’s ID (due to the nature of IDs from a specific country), {color:#4c9aff}*the next most preferred method would be manual review*{color} (i.e., a human reviewing the user’s ID / photo to determine their gender). In practice, this could look something like someone on the Bolt side reviewing the relevant documents and then marking the user’s gender on their profile in Admin (to the extent that this is clear / they have reasonable confidence of the same) - however, {color:#ff5630}*grateful for your thoughts on how this would be achieved in practice*{color}.


*Centralisation and retention*

I have recently been asked on a separate ticket ([+LSS-43036+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-43036]) to advise on this from a France POV. It would be preferable, to the extent possible, to try and {color:#4c9aff}*take a centralised / global approach*{color} to this type of verification ‘as standard’, and then assess whether we need to adapt it for certain countries.
In terms of where we keep gender data, we should also ensure that we are {color:#4c9aff}*keeping it in Admin*{color} (rather than, for example, separate Google sheets) - this is not a Privacy point _per se_, but would be more efficient from a records retention perspective.

*The issue of inaccuracy*

One of the main issues with collecting data on a user’s gender is that data protection law requires Bolt to ensure that the data it keeps is accurate. Unfortunately, gender is an increasingly complex concept and so by collecting this data we run the risk of being accused of specifying the ‘wrong’ gender for certain users.
There is no easy way to get around this issue - however, by using the methods specified above (i.e., as a first port of call, seeing if a user’s ID specifies their gender, and if not resorting to manual review) would help to mitigate the risk here by assessing gender in a way that seems rationale and would fall within the reasonable expectation of users.
Although I appreciate that this would not be a perfect system (as people can make mistakes), I would also flag that AI tools are likely to encounter similar accuracy issues - at the very least human review would be more within the user’s expectations and so would be more defensible from a Privacy POV.

*Lawfulness and transparency*

[~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] has asked separately whether we have a valid legal basis to collect gender data in this context - in short, {color:#4c9aff}*we can argue that we do provided that we are not overly invasive with the data we collect*{color}. In other words:
* We can rely on Bolt’s _legitimate interest_ (rather than, for example, separate consent) to process such data. This approach would most closely align with what is set out in our rider privacy notices.
* To rely on this legal basis, the data we are collecting must be strictly necessary for this purpose. As set out above, IMO we do not need to scan faces to collect this data, but can instead rely on gender as specified in an ID and otherwise manual review. This would be more defensible from a Privacy POV.
[~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] also asked whether we need to update the privacy notices - the short answer is {color:#4c9aff}*yes, but not significantly*{color}. I have already discussed with Gab and there are some tweaks we would need to make for jurisdictions where this is launched, but this is something we could arrange as needed.

See tähendab, et ei FIE, OÜ ega muu jur isik platvormil teenust osutada ei saa.Seadusandja mõtte kohaselt on selle teenuse osutamine mõeldud eelkõige füüsilisele isikule lisategevuseks, mitte tema elatusallikas. Kuna isikul tuleks kogu oma sissetulek ausalt deklareerida ja seda 1 x aastas tuludeklaratsiooni esitades, siis loodigi EMTAs selle mugavamaks deklareerimiseks ettevõtluskonto. Ettevõtluskonto pangas on eraisiku konto kus ta saab kirja panna oma lisateenistuse (a’la müüsin 10 tomatit, 7 kurki, osutasin taksoteenust), mille alusel on maksuametil parem ülevaade isiku täiendavatest sissetulekutest ja vaikne lootus, et deklareeritaks ka taksoteenuse osutamine. See tähendab, et ÜTS järgi tegelevad eraisikud ettevõtlusega olemata ise seejuures kantud erinevatesse ettevõtete registritesse kui OÜ, AS, MTÜ jne jne.Infoühiskonna teenuse osutamise võimaldamine OÜ-le või FIE-le eeldab iseseisva taksoveo tegevusloa ja selle alusel sõidukikaardi omamist. Sellisel viisil töötavad täna paljud Tallinki või ForusTakso (ex Tulika Takso) sildi all, makstes kaubamärgi kasutamise, eetri ja saadavate tellimuste eest, kuid igaüks on iseseisev ettevõtja.Selleks, et võimaldada OÜ-del, FIE-del jne infoühiskonna teenust osutada, jõuame kahe äriühinguvahelise kokkuleppeni (vt eelmist lõiku) ja tegelikult seadusandja mõtte kadumiseni. Mõistame, et Bolt sooviks vabaneda võimalikult suures ulatuses vastutusest ja lükata see teenuse osutajale. Täna on Bolt siiski olnud sunnitud looma juriidilise keha ja tunnistama end taksoettevõtjaks (omades taksoveo tegevusluba), kes liidab enda külge eraisikutest teenuse osutajad ja teeb nendele ülekanded osutatud sõitude eest. Tegelikult saaks siin rääkida töösuhtest, on riike, kus Bolt loetaksegi tegelikult tööandjaks.Pika jutu kokkuvõtteks: Bolt platvormil saab teenust osutada ainult eraisik, olenemata kas tal on ettevõtluskonto või mitte.
Kas siin saaks ja võiks teha ühistranspordiseaduse muudatuse, seda oskavad vaid juristid kommenteerida ja kuna see algatus toona tuli otse riigikoguliikmetelt, siis tuleks neil ka sinna pöörduda.

_T&Cs_

~ The chain of communication that concerns the advice on VT ~

Loi Nguyen approached the Privacy Team to inquire about the collection of temporary addresses. Among the most important purposes for such collection, Loi mentioned better cooperation with the Law Enforcement Authorities since majority of drivers are moving to bigger cities solely for work purposes but are not permanent residents of that region. In this case, leads would be requested to provide such information at the stage of providing driver personal information rather than payouts and other financial data.

Alon and I have analysed the collection of temporary addresses from the VT law perspective. That is the [advice|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07TB1BBRA7/p1732636089222909] that I provided:

“_First and foremost, while Vietnamese data protection laws outline certain principles (such as data minimisation, accuracy, etc.), these principles are closely linked to the consent-driven nature of the PDPD. For instance, as specified in Art.3 (4) of the_ [_PDPD_|https://eurochamvn.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Decree-13-2023-PDPD_EN_clean.pdf]_: “Personal data that are obtained must be appropriate and limited to the scope and purposes of processing.”  Consequently, Vietnam operates as a consent-based market, where data privacy primarily depends on an individual's awareness and voluntary agreement to have their data processed. Therefore, even though there is no fundamental restriction on collecting temporary addresses in theory, we must consider the following points:_

* _Drivers must be made aware of the fact that temporary addresses are collected and for what purpose._
* _Drivers are informed about the organisations/ entities that such information is shared with._
* _And other standard requirements imposed when processing the data._

_Hence, having taken all of that into account, my advice is that the collection of temporary addresses shall not constitute a substantial burden to Bolt’s privacy-related operations. In practice, however, the following actions are suggested:_

* _When collecting the temporary addresses, in the Google Sheet or any other format that the drivers will utilise to provide us with their temporary addresses, we shall clearly specify that “The collection of temporary addresses serves the purpose of a facilitated communication between Bolt and the drivers”._
* _The rest of the information is to be found within our Privacy Notices._”

Subsequently, Loi was [advised|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C06RVM2D0SY/p1732705979202099?thread_ts=1732699175.644799&cid=C06RVM2D0SY] to slightly change the wording of the purpose sentence.

Hey [~accountid:5bb7726959e46d7be31aad4c] - thanks for raising this topic.

In short, yes, a woman to woman category (and anything similar) is prone to scrutiny and claims of ‘discrimination’, as you mention. Bolt therefore ought to assess the suitability of launching any ‘woman to woman’ category on a per market basis, consulting in particular with the local regulatory, safety and operations teams, whilst also involving local legal counsel (to keep them in the loop). 

I recommend you pick this up with the regulatory team to take this forward and to determine whether this needs reviewing on a per market basis.

From my side, here’s some general considerations:

* There are three sources of complaint: public sentiment, transport regulators and consumer protection agencies. 
* Public sentiment will escalate the likelihood of complaints to transport regulators and consumer protection agencies. For example, in some markets there is currently publicity and debate over what the phrase ‘woman’ includes. In other markets, this will be less sensitive.
* Transport regulatory authorities may or may not have rules on these topics, particularly when members of the public can ‘hail’ a vehicle from the street (i.e. a taxi). Other regulators may provide express rights for drivers to deny passengers.
* Consumer protection agencies will always have some ability to deal with what they consider to be discriminatory so there is no need for a lengthy review of this topic, beyond quick research from local operations and regulatory teams to see whether similar issues have arisen in the market before.

Where there is concern that the category may be scrutinised for any of the above reasons, Bolt has scope to choose to launch the category and mitigate any scrutiny by, for example, preparing PR responses to validate (or withdraw) the category; based on safety issues, demand and so on. Or, Bolt could choose to speak with transport regulators in advance, if this is recommended by the local transport reg. team. Where the category has been launched, Bolt can review these topics and then reach out to transport regulators if there is a major concern.

Having a licence pulled in entirety does seem quite severe; the local regulatory team are best placed to comment on it, but where Bolt has a good relationship with a transport regulatory I would hope for a ‘dialogue’ rather than a harsh sanction.

Finally, I’m aware that these categories sometimes don’t actually address the safety risks that they purport to solve. If Bolt becomes aware that a ‘woman to woman’ actually *_increases_* the risk of harm to women, then the business should urgently review whether it ought to be pulled.

I hope that’s helpful. I’ll close this ticket but let me know if you need any further input - thanks 👌

_In accordance with what was discussed, I am sending our analysis regarding the concerns raised by BOLT about the rejection of our Clause Three - DATA PROTECTION._

_Let me begin by highlighting what our clause specifies about the roles of BOLT (as the Data Processor) and MAPFRE (as the Data Controller):_

*_“This clause regulates (i) the data processing that BOLT, as the Data Processor, will carry out on behalf of MAPFRE, MAPFRE VIDA, and MAPFRE SANTANDER, as Data Controllers, regarding personal data necessary to provide the contracted services (hereinafter referred to as 'the Services'); and (ii) the security and confidentiality obligations that BOLT must comply with in relation to the Information (as defined below) provided by MAPFRE, MAPFRE VIDA, and MAPFRE SANTANDER or to which BOLT has access.”_*

_When reviewing the objections raised, it is unclear what position BOLT intends to assert. Specifically:_

# _In point 2 (below), BOLT claims that they are obligated to act as a_ *_Data Processor_*_._
# _However, in point 3, BOLT states that, by default, they always act as a_ *_Data Controller_*_._

_This creates a contradiction, making their stance difficult to understand. We kindly request that this point be clarified and justified, preferably with comments added directly to the contract._

_For context, here is the objection raised by BOLT:_



_“Clause 3: DATA PROTECTION_

_This clause contradicts the basic data protection framework between Bolt and its business customers._

_Bolt is required to act as a Data Processor and comply with strict obligations under Article 28 GDPR._

_By default, however, Bolt always acts as a Data Controller and does not agree to the restrictive requirements of Article 28 GDPR, as they are deemed unrealistic._

_We must reject Clause 3 and ensure that data processing is governed by Section 4 of the General T&Cs, which clarifies that Bolt acts as a Data Controller.”_



_Our Position:_

_The Data Controller is the entity responsible—MAPFRE, in this case—for making decisions about the processing of personal data. The Controller determines the purposes for which data will be used, how it will be processed, and which security measures will be applied._

_The Data Processor, in this case, BOLT, processes personal data solely on behalf of the Data Controller. The Processor is typically an external third party, meaning an entity that processes data on behalf of the Controller._

[~accountid:61f116071c42100069544016], could you have a look at the proposed solution and confirm if we can proceed with implementing it?

The problem discussed comes from the edge cases where both the *user* and *third party* are to be potential claimants which is not considered one of the possible scenarios within the current setup. 

Currently, the logic is as follows:
In the Assessment tool, the agent marks down any Injuries that have occurred as a result of an incident (to user or third party), and whether there were any damages (to Bolt rental, or a third party vehicle). Then, if a third party was marked to be injured or their vehicle was damaged, *or* if the user sustained injuries, the agent is asked to look through the list of “blockers” which allows us to determine whether the Insurance form needs to be shown or not:

!Screenshot 2024-12-09 at 13.52.30.png|width=492,height=68,alt="Screenshot 2024-12-09 at 13.52.30.png"!

Below this field, we show the blockers, such as _“user being under 18 years old”_ etc. based on the aforementioned choice of “user” or “third party”. That is the scenario that we want to cover:

!Screenshot 2024-12-09 at 13.55.58.png|width=497,height=678,alt="Screenshot 2024-12-09 at 13.55.58.png"!

The proposed solution is to separate the list into two separate columns and advise agents to *_select “Yes” only if all claimant types have applicable blockers if there are multiple claimant types._* This way, we can ensure that if the user received small injuries but there was also a damage to third party, we still correctly suggest escalating.

!Screenshot 2024-12-04 at 11.38.25.png|width=521,height=614,alt="Screenshot 2024-12-04 at 11.38.25.png"!

Please, let me know if this makes sense. Thank you!

*When a courier is blocked we communicate to the fleet. Is there a legal requirement to communicate to the courier as well?*



From [+Lisette Suik+|mailto:lisette.suik@bolt.eu]



So, Article 11 and Recital 49 from the [PWD|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/2831/oj] sets out that *persons performing platform work* have to receive “a written statement of reasons” when they are blocked. Persons performing platform work = include fleet couriers as well.  They also have a right to appeal the decision.

Since the PWD *has* *_not_* *been implemented yet,* so we don’t know how exactly member states will regulate how the blocking message should be sent, then we have taken the approach that the “written statement of reasons” should be in the same format as we use to block couriers right now - the general obligation to notify of blocking arises from [P2B Article 4|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A32019R1150].  The notice has to be done via email and contain: (i) reason why they were blocked (e.g. didn’t deliver order), (ii) how this action breached our TCs,  (iii) if this was based on client’s complaint, then email has to reference that (i.e. “we’ve received a complaint), (iv) how they can appeal this decision.

So, in conclusion, although we do not (yet) have an obligation to notify fleet couriers of why they were blocked, then we have taken the approach to notify them already now.  Although it could be argued that we should not notify fleet couriers due to reclass reasons, then there are two things to consider: (i) if a courier is blocked and receives an email with a clear reason + reference to how they can appeal, it might mean they are less likely to get angry and complain (vs if they did not receive any comms). (ii) if we block a fleet courier, we also send comms to the fleet (i.e. the actual contractual party) - so that it’s clear that we still contract with the fleet, we just send the courier the notification as an administrative step.

Hi! I reviewed the comms and form and for the most part it looks fine. I would however modify the confirmation text at the end of the form as follows:

_I hereby confirm that I will transport the tree securely, ensuring it is properly fixed to prevent any damage to passenger and vehicle interior_ {color:#ff5630}_while adhering to all traffic laws, in particular to the requirements regarding the carriage of goods_{color}_._

The law states that cargo must be placed, fastened and covered in accordance with its characteristics and packaging in such a manner that it does not jeopardise the people or the environment, does not cause pecuniary harm or obstruct traffic (§ 34 (6) of the [Traffic Act|https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/eli/519082024009/consolide#:~:text=%C2%A0(6)%20The%20cargo%20must%20be%20placed%2C%20fastened%20and%20covered%20in%20accordance%20with%20its%20characteristics%20and%20packaging%20in%20such%20a%20manner%20that%20it%20does%20not%20jeopardise%20the%20people%20or%20the%20environment%2C%20does%20not%20cause%20pecuniary%20harm%20or%20obstruct%20traffic.]), and further requirements are laid down in a [regulation|https://www.riigiteataja.ee/akt/124042020005]. While the drivers are already obligated to follow such rules thanks to the T&Cs, I recommend having them reconfirm this in the form. That way Bolt would not be regarded as promoting unsafe carriage of cargo.

* What is the purpose of our collaboration with the counterparty? What services do they provide?

The counterparty will act as a scout, or field sales agent, to actively search for interested drivers and help them to register on our portal. We don’t share any details of drivers who are already in our funnel, they sign up the ones they find through their network or on the street.

* What data are we supposed to make accessible to them and how?

We only share the status of the drivers they sign up. Scouts are paid by drivers they register using their referral code who complete X trips, but currently they have no visibility of the flow. Therefore we share with them the first name, the phone number and the status of the drivers they register using their Referral Code. The status can be: stuck as lead, declined because of XYZ, accepted and how many trip they’ve done to date and if they achieved their target.

This data is currently shared on a PDF by email generated via Looker. In the future we are looking to share these details directly through the app.

* Will the counterparty use any sub-processors?

It’s possible that counterparty has other scouts working for them and will let them know if one of their drivers is stuck somewhere so they can follow up. But majority of time they are individual freelancers.

*** *Find vulnerabilities or weaknesses in our verification process*

Analysed label usage for the period of 02/12/2024 - 08/12/2024

+My drink was spilled usage:+

* 20/50 times the label was used correctly, meaning whether it was the only label used for a drink spill (as supposed) or it was a justified combination of spilled drink + damaged food ([good example of a soaked burger|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/485201656]).
* 30/50 times the label was used incorrectly:
** Often times, it is used incorrectly in a combination with “My order was damaged” - it is actually not clear from the photo that in addition to spilled drink, also the food was damaged. For example, if only a bag from the outside is photographed, it is impossible to say that it wasn’t a bag for drinks solely, but also included some food. Moreover, if a bag without any food items inside is photographed, this should be considered as spilled drink only, not a damaged order. 
** Even in cases where clearly only a drink was spilled, damaged order label was also used in combination.

+My order was damaged:+

* 38/50 times label was used correctly, meaning food was actually damaged by the drink spill or deformed during transportation. Please note that correct usage also includes cases without a photo proof, so the label was determined based on the claim (8/38).
* 10/50 times, label was used incorrectly with a combination with “My drink was spilled” as the only label should have been “My drink was spilled”. _(2/50 times label was used incorrectly due to another issue e.g delay but this is irrelevant in this context)_



+Conclusion:+

Agents tend to use “My drink was spilled” and “My order was damaged” incorrectly in a combination, without differentiating if it was actually just a drink spill, which is the issue in most cases.

*I do not see the need to schedule the task for our own Payouts*, we should call the {{rental_car_billing}} API directly, instead of scheduling a task. (Call API, or maybe better, send an event.)
* This is where we want to add the API call to {{rental-car-billing}}: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/2fb5896112bd514228f03e9acf6872db2bf2206b/src/platform/commerce/billing_payout/main/service/RentalCarPayoutService.ts#L30-L33|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/2fb5896112bd514228f03e9acf6872db2bf2206b/src/platform/commerce/billing_payout/main/service/RentalCarPayoutService.ts#L30-L33] 

h2. The code on Rental Car Billing side

* Listen to an event, and create a record - very symmetrical to Partner Payment events - follow from here: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/8d4075ef7609d335c0b38c6b17a1263e7fe658b4/src/rental/carsharing/rental_car_billing/main/Bootstrap.ts#L140-L141|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/8d4075ef7609d335c0b38c6b17a1263e7fe658b4/src/rental/carsharing/rental_car_billing/main/Bootstrap.ts#L140-L141] 
(We support *Payments* (partners paying us), but now we want to add records for *Payouts* as well (us paying partners).)

h2. Implementation details

* Listen to an event from Billing Payout, and register it as an Organic Event (like Partner Payments)
* Create a record in DB of a new type, similar to Partner Payments
* Don’t export the record (use {{balance_state: IGNORE}}) (because {{billing_payout}} updates {{invoicing_balance}})
* The execution should be idempotent, so:
** If the record is found, then the organic event shoud still succeed
** If the record is found, then the record shouldn’t be created again (DB’s unique index constraint should somehow prevent it - utilize {{organic_event_id}})

Answers to Laura’s questions:

* *_Do we need to set the same risk as in the main case?_*
** The case should be escalated to the Safety tier by following the 🚨 [Escalating cases to Safety|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/73261?country=global&language=en] guidelines:
*** Choose the applicable *Safety severity level* based on the list of safety events
**** If you're not sure about the exact event, choose the closest severity level
*** Change the tier to *Safety*
*** Unassign the case from yourself
*** No further action is necessary
* *_Is there any official instruction on how agents should handle the blocking ticket cases?_* 
** Every Safety case is handled by following the workflows in the KB. When the driver gets blocked - the safety agent will *always* send a message to the driver informing them about the blocking. So we would only receive a driver’s ticket asking about a safety blocking if they *didn’t notice our previous message*, where we already informed them. 
** When the safety agent receives an escalated ticket about the blocking, they don’t need to take *any additional actions*, as the case is already resolved and the driver was already informed. All they need to do is to find the case due to which the driver was blocked (additionally, find the outgoing ticket which was sent to the driver to inform about the blocking), and *one more time let the driver know why they are blocked*. There’s no need for instructions or processes to handle such cases, as it is a common practice. 
* *_Should the safety template comments also be left in these tickets?_*
** As mentioned above, the case was already resolved and the additional ticket received from the driver requires *only to repeat the information that was already provided*. No additional comments or templates are required.

        FROM commerce_finance_spark.finance_model_payment_transaction_fee_v2 fee
        where transaction_date >= timestamp '2024-11-01' and  transaction_date < '2024-12-01'

        GROUP BY 1) sq{code}

Flow accepted by OPS team: 
If there are no clear evidence in the Admin (battery drop) or user haven’t shared any photos or videos showing the issue CS will:

{{Step 1:}}
Check 3 past ride and if any feedback regarding same issue was provided:
*Yes* - problem marker + refund;
*No* - step 2

{{Step 2:}}
Check future ride and if any feedback regarding same issue was provided:
*Yes* -  Problem marker + refund
*No* - Step 3

{{Step 3 }}
Check how many refunds user received in the last month regarding the same issue.
*0-3* - refund the user
*3+* - inform the user that refund will not be provided.

less than 100m covered: Refund 100% of the trip price
more than 100m covered: Refund 50% of the trip price

Hey, [~accountid:60a7a9683fae6f0068ff79a0]! 

Coming back to you regarding the questions you raised.

{quote}In some cases, riders reach out to us complaining that the driver has demanded money to bring the item back (usually in average 60-70 EUR). Can we have instructions what to educate the users in such cases?{quote}

The general rule in cases like these is that the rider and driver need to resolve such situations themselves. Bolt is a platform that facilitates a connection between riders and drivers, and we do not bear responsibility for lost items. Drivers can ask for a finders fee since they are spending their time and fuel to get back to the rider, however, whether to pay or not is the rider’s choice and depends on their goodwill. The rider’s decision should not affect the successful return of the lost item. At the same time, there are countries where situations like these are regulated by law. Because these are low-volume cases and it’s not urgent, we won’t be making any content updates to this article in regards to this for now as the Process Excellence team needs to take a look first. As soon as that’s done, and we’ve acquired all the relevant information and data, we’ll make any updates that are necessary. 



{quote}In the lost phone article, there’s an instruction to ask the rider to send their alternative number so we can share it with the driver if needed. If they send us a phone number, and tell that this is my friend’s number you can share it with the driver as alternative, is it ok to share the phone number in terms of compliance?{quote}

It’s quite natural that if a user loses their phone, they’ll leave their friend's or relative’s phone number as a contact, so, yes, if the rider gives explicit written consent to sharing the provided alternative phone number, it is okay to do so, considering whether the process requires it. The rider needs to ensure that the owner of the phone number is aware of this sharing and that consent to share their phone number comes from the owner. 

I hope I’ve managed to address everything. If there’s anything else, feel free to raise a new ticket and we’ll get to it. 

Thank you, and have a nice day! 🙂

Thanks [~accountid:712020:0f7a089b-3b06-423b-844c-6e5ac370aa1e] - Zoom’s comments are not especially surprising given their approach to negotiations to date. It seems there is not much more scope for arguing for the inclusion of these provisions. As such, {color:#36b37e}*we do not have anything further to propose from the Privacy side*{color}. 

This does not necessarily act as a blocker to signing the agreement - ultimately, it is now a business decision re whether to proceed. However, please not the following from my previous comment, as before making the final decision {color:#ff5630}*the business needs to be aware that it will be accepting the following risks should something ‘go wrong’*{color}:

* Let’s say that Zoom suffered a personal data breach that affected Bolt customer data, and we discovered that Bolt needed to notify the data protection regulators about this:
** *Delayed notification / fines*: In this example, Bolt would need to notify the regulators within a specified timeframe. However, the unamended DPA does not set a specific deadline by which Zoom should provide Bolt with all the necessary information to do so. This means that Bolt may not be able to notify the regulators in time, which could damage our relationship with them. In such circumstances, the regulators could also order corrective action and/or fines against Bolt.
** *Difficult recovery*: The unamended DPA does not include pro-Bolt indemnities for any data protection non-compliance by Zoom. Referring again to the above example, if the data breach was Zoom’s fault and Bolt was fined by a regulator as a result of this, it would be difficult for Bolt to recover the fine amount from Zoom. Also, given the liability cap of 240k in the main agreement, even if Bolt could recover some money from Zoom, this may not be sufficient to cover Bolt’s total liability (as a data protection regulator could fine Bolt up to EUR 20m / 4% of worldwide turnover).
** *Increased risk of non-cooperation / costs of investigation*: If Bolt then wanted to ensure that this kind of incident did not happen again, under the unamended DPA Bolt would have to bear the costs of investigating Zoom’s data protection compliance and making recommendations. This would result in further financial liability on Bolt’s side.
* Please note that the above is a snapshot of the risks that Bolt could be exposed to by accepting the unamended DPA, particularly in light of the lack of a pro-Bolt indemnity and the inclusion of a 240k liability cap. We do not ordinarily accept these in agreements that we are negotiating.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
If the business is ok with these risks, then it can proceed with signing the agreement without any of our proposed changes to the DPA.
{panel}

Hey,

We have a netting in Georgia.

Through commission netting, your campaigns/bonuses/compensations are reflected as a discount from your commission, instead of each having their individual invoices. Simply, your commission is reduced in the amount of your campaigns/bonuses/compensations - ensuring a more clear invoicing process, and less invoicing noise.

For example, previously you would see a commission of 416.91GEL and separate bonus lines of 11GEL on your invoice, which totaled up to 361.92GEL. Now, you would only see a single row of commission in the amount of 361.92GEL, meaning the calculation is already done in the background.



TLDR:

* We have commission netting in Georgia
* For that reason we do not issue

For context, when a third party was marked to be injured or their vehicle was damaged in the, *or* if the user sustained injuries, the agent is asked to look through the list of “blockers” (shown under {{Select YES...}} field) which allows us to determine whether the Insurance form needs to be shown or not. The problem discussed comes from the edge cases where both the *user* and *third party* are to be potential claimants which is not considered one of the possible scenarios within the current setup. 

The proposed solution is to change the layout of the “blockers”: separate the list into two separate columns, and advise agents to *_select “Yes” only if all claimant types have applicable blockers if there are multiple claimant types._* This way, we can ensure that if the user received small injuries but there was also a damage to third party, we still correctly suggest escalating.
