Hi, below you can find some answers to your questions which I hope makes it more clear. I will also update the KB to clearly state what Safety is expected to do. 

* *_Do we need to set the same risk as in the main case?_*
** The case should be escalated to the Safety tier by following the 🚨 [Escalating cases to Safety|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/73261?country=global&language=en] guidelines:
*** Choose the applicable *Safety severity level* based on the list of safety events
**** If you're not sure about the exact event, choose the closest severity level
*** Change the tier to *Safety*
*** Unassign the case from yourself
*** No further action is necessary
* *_Is there any official instruction on how agents should handle the blocking ticket cases?_*
** Every Safety case is handled by following the workflows in the KB. When the driver gets blocked - the safety agent will *always* send a message to the driver informing them about the blocking. So we would only receive a driver’s ticket asking about a safety blocking if they *didn’t notice our previous message*, where we already informed them.
** When the safety agent receives an escalated ticket about the blocking, they don’t need to take *any additional actions*, as the case is already resolved and the driver was already informed. All they need to do is to find the case due to which the driver was blocked (additionally, find the outgoing ticket which was sent to the driver to inform about the blocking), and *one more time let the driver know why they are blocked*. There’s no need for instructions or processes to handle such cases, as it is a common practice.
* *_Should the safety template comments also be left in these tickets?_*
** As mentioned above, the case was already resolved and the additional ticket received from the driver requires *only to repeat the information that was already provided*. No additional comments or templates are required.

Please note that the information provided in the links shared below is sustained and emanates from a “City hall warning (published [here|https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/aviso/13367-2016-75624025]) who proceeded to a review of the  _Regulation of Opening Hours for Public Sales and Service Establishments in the Municipality of Lisbon_, also already shared by Bryan.

The law ([https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/portaria/154-469022|https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/portaria/154-469022]) that you shared with a definition of “Loja de Conveniência“ was revoked and therefore is no longer in force. In accordance with my research, there isn’t any other “Portaria“ with a new definition of “Loja de Conveniência“ besides the definition that is defined in article 7 of the “City Hall Warning“: _“Para efeitos do presente regulamento, entende-se por loja de conveniência, os estabelecimentos_ *_inseridos no grupo VI que procedam à venda de bebidas_*_, independentemente da sua atividade principal, e que_ *_não correspondam ao grupo I_*_, devidamente legalizados.“_

In our opinion, since (i) your CAE does not fit in Group I, and also (ii) as said by CML the law does not specify what’s the schedule allowed for your CAE, and (iii) Bolt Market sells drinks, our conclusion remains the same.

 Therefore, you have 3 options with different levels of risk:

* +you maintain the current working hours/schedule.+ Please note that the condominium can start to control the working hours or Bolt Market has a “surprise“ inspection. if Bolt Market is not complying with the permitted schedule and one of the hypotheses happens, this situation can lead to a fine up of to €25,000. Also, as a complementary sanction, the authorities can also close the store for a period not exceeding 1 year. Looking at the lease agreement, although we know that you have a good relationship with the landlord, not complying with the working hours - in extreme - could also lead to a breach of the agreement, (please see section 6 called “utilities“) and also point 4.1.6. of the General Terms. The willingness to do so, will depend on the landlord’s initiative
* +you comply with the working schedule+ - from 6AM to 10PM every week;
* +you request a schedule extension to CML.+ Here the risk associated is the extension being refused by CML.

Thank you.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *11 November 2024.*

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

Hey [~accountid:712020:1e9398f2-efcd-4dcd-8ece-28e6f8578e37],

I do not see a blocker to deploy KPIs for scheduled rides:

* *Regulatory perspective*: 
** The RH regulation in Malta would appear not to include any obligation for electronic platforms with impact in this project. 
** In fact, this regulation includes a general obligation for operators not to refuse services, except in limited cases: “_19. An operator shall not have the right to refuse to provide light passenger transport services to any hirer except on reasonable grounds, including, when it is clear from his demeanour, that the hirer is under the influence of drugs or alcohol or where the safety and security of the driver may be at risk._” 
** I can see that max number of unfulfilled Scheduled Rides in the last 12 weeks is only 3 and we should be aware that drivers have the right to refuse services on the situation indicated above.
* *Reclassification perspective*:
** IMO the risk is low since the KPIs are not linked with a determination of what work is to be done and how it is to be carried out. Instead, it is based on the result of the previous work and engagement with the Bolt Platform.
* *Terms and conditions:*
** MT t&c establish that drives “retain the sole right to determine when you are providing the Transportation Services. You shall accept, decline or ignore Transportation Services requests made by Passengers at your own choosing.” Even though the deployment of KPIs may result in suspending access of some drivers to scheduled rides, it would not lead to a suspension or blocking to the platform and hence drivers still maintain their right to determine when to provide transportation services. 

Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Dear Lilia, 

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *10 November 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Communications with the Customer Support of Bolt from August 2023.*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/de-de/privacy/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/de-de/privacy/?category=rides|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

Safety Impact document will be compiled on a quarterly basis, *starting with looking at the whole 2024 as the Q4 ends,* to see the trends and gather feedback.

* Report to be based on the damages recorded by OPS solely. 
* The incidents that have injuries, or that have no damage to the Bolt drive vehicle _(_Faulty equipment, Damages to 3rd parties, Behavioural etc.) will be tracked separately, and presented as EFR.
* The glossary needs to be added to explain the metrics.

:loading: *Pending:* Germany OPS Sheet doesn’t have some of the details needed for calculations. [~accountid:712020:435d7fc1-7078-4aa9-b2a5-32758f7e11e4] is looking into it. More notes [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/19gXpPiIzGVWp7qM13jiTbNp1LDqNrtgtP-EhrZV3twE/edit?tab=t.0].

+Glossary+
*Total GMV,* from [here|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/11309?City=&Timeframe+Picker=Month&Created+Date=2024-06&Country=&Partner+Code=&Flow+Type=]

*Total Estimated costs,* the sum of estimated costs, based on Damage cost estimate. 

*Total Actual Repair costs*, the sum of actual costs for repairs, based on Actual repair costs.

*Total Final Cost,* mainly based on Actual repair cost, and Estimate where Actual cost is missing.

*Total Deductible,* a sum of all Deductible charged.

*Total GMV loss,* based on Total Loss.

*Total Days in Repair*



*Calculations for each entry*

*OPEX,* taken as 1€ as a placeholder.

*GMV Per day per Model,* constant of 50€.

*Final Cost* = _Actual Repair cost (if missing, then Estimate Repair Cost) - Deductible Charged_

*Total Loss* = _Cost (Excl. Deductible) + (GMV Per Day Per Model * Days in repair)_



*Damage Rate (% of Orders)* = Damages / Orders * 100

*Damage traceability (cases)*, shows the proportion of cases where we know who is responsible party. Based on the Fault field. 

*Damage traceability (costs),* a sum of final costs where the party at fault is known.

[~accountid:557058:b2aaf2b9-4465-40fe-b31b-1711dbe61946] that explanation was what we already told the client and it does not work for them. Please note the following:

# According to BB teams companies usually want a single invoice for all rides taken in a month. It makes it easier on their accounting/financial processes side and this is where the resale model comes in and there is one Bolt VAT number issuing a single invoice for all rides/countries where rides are taken.
# From a VAT perspective what should happen in case of rides taken abroad is that Bolt issues one invoice per jurisdiction with local VAT. This would mean that there are multiple invoices instead of one, and that the client should go to each jurisdiction and claim the local VAT back which is quite burdensome. 
# To make this easier, Bolt pays for the rides taken in other jurisdictions and includes these in a single invoice as expenses borne on behalf of the client in other jurisdictions, and asks for a refund of these costs which is not subject to VAT. The total costs to be refunded include ride price plus VAT, but because it is included in the single invoice issued by Bolt, the client cannot recover the VAT on it (only way to do that was by receiving a single invoice for each jurisdiction). 
# Most of the clients do not seem to have a problem with this because of different reasons. They may not be able to recover it under the applicable legal provisions, they may not care because the amounts are not material, or they prefer getting one invoice than receiving multiple invoices and going through the hassle of filing VAT refund requests in different countries. 
# Contrary to most of the clients, this one already has this procedure in place in different countries and for them it is more beneficial to get multiple invoices. That is why they want a different setup which allows them to recover part of the costs. However, we do not have this capability at the moment and it is a rare situation so wondering if it makes sense to request development.

Thank you [~accountid:6270f0bd807e0000691b79bb] . Let me respond to your questions you shared below:

* {color:#bf2600}_Can we rely on this existing hard opt-in consent to start targeting users with location-based comms or do we need something additional?_{color}

For now, definitely yes. Privacy will try to assess if consent can be avoided, but its best to rely on consent.

* {color:#bf2600}_Do we need to update existing T&Cs or is this already covered since the consent already exists and some users have already provided consent?_{color}

It will depend if we want to obtain consent. 

Currently, we only inform users that we can use the following data for marketing personalisation: date and time, pick-up and drop-off addresses, journey distances and routes.

If you are intending to use *live location data* as well, we will need either to update our privacy notices, or inform the users separately. Per [this page|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/3589997095/Real-Time+Geolocation+Tracking+for+Lifecycle+Marketing#Using-Real-Time-Geolocation-for-Lifecycle-Marketing], the Rider LCM team should have a marketing plan to obtain “Travelling” consents. If we clearly inform the user at this stage that we want to use their live data, than we can avoid the need to update our privacy notices specifically for this activity.

* {color:#bf2600}_Can we use the same type of consent for Rentals and Business comms as well?_{color}

We can target Riders with information on our mobility offers (i.e. rentals, micromobility, Bolt Business).

* {color:#bf2600}_This existing travelling consent only covers push and email as channels. Do we need to add it for in-apps as well, or can we treat location-based in-apps similar to other in-apps, i.e. exempt from consents?_{color}

We definitely need to keep consent for in-app as long as we rely on consent for other channels. As I understand, the logic of consent here is that its needed to use live location, and consent is requested for this purpose specifically.

if we can unblock using live location for marketing personalisation without consent, we will be able to extend this to all channels, including in-App.

* {color:#bf2600}_Is there anything additional from legal point of view that we need to keep in mind/take care of before we start targeting users with this consent?_{color}

The privacy team must review the text of consent before you target the users.

*To sum up:*

# Using live location to personalise marketing is possible - you are not blocked. Where we want to use live location - we should stick to consent.
# To ensure the lawfulness of the activity, privacy will need to review the consent text.
# Privacy will try to reevaluate our lawful basis, to check if it is possible to rely on an alternative lawful basis. *Let's align here on specific timeframes so we can effectively support you.* Best for privacy is to work on this somewhere in Q1 2025.

{noformat}with after_discount as (
	select year, month, product_servicename,  sum(line_item_unblended_cost) + sum(discount_total_discount) as cost

	where year >= 2023 and month >= 1
	AND line_item_usage_account_id = '451613234044'
	and product_product_name = 'Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud'
	group by 1,2,3
),
only_tagged_price as (
	select year, month, product_servicename, sum(line_item_unblended_cost) as cost
	from ng_public.aws_cost_metrics
	where year >= 2023 and month >= 1
	AND line_item_usage_account_id = '451613234044'
	and line_item_line_item_type not in ('Tax', 'SavingsPlanNegation')
	and product_product_name = 'Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud'
	group by 1,2,3
),
ec2_discount_percentage as (
  select a.year, a.month, a.product_servicename, (a.cost / b.cost), a.cost, b.cost
  from after_discount as a
  left join only_tagged_price  as b
  on b.month = a.month and b.year = a.year and a.product_servicename = b.product_servicename
)
select * from ec2_discount_percentage order by 1 desc, 2 desc{noformat}

Hey [~accountid:62d7b457807cf6f78ca9d117], I give you the general guidance we have given to the central teams regarding blocks based on police requests (I guess this is meant by authority here):

* generally speaking we do not block user for sole investigatory police requests

There is scope to do it for the following cases:

* user is involved in a safety incident during a ride which was matched on our platform (typical safety event)
* investigation about fake licenses, regulatory details
* clear instruction to block this person by police for xyz reason

We definitely don’t care about the following:

* user involved in crimes with a Bolt branded car outside of the usage of the app
* user involved in any other activities outside of the app

Other exceptions where a legal assessment needs to happen before a block:

* blocks for reasons which could affect Bolt’s reputation and brand (e.g. involved in a crime with a Bolt branded car)

For *the duration of safety blocks* specifically I loop in [~accountid:5d0c8f1621a5d30bc4e096a8] but as far as I know, we block users permanently if there is physical harm or physical threat. 
If we block people for missing or faked licenses we frame this as a “_pause or lack of access_” which is not a suspension or termination in a legal sense. This means the user is blocked until they do XYZ. The block depends on the actions of the user. If they upload their new licenses the access restriction will be uplifted. 

I hope this helps a bit. If you have any further questions, please shoot!

Thanks [~accountid:62b2cf3c0c77011bdfdcdbcd] - I assume that Bolt (Romania) is the _Beneficiary_ under this agreement, and the vendor is the _Provider_? If so, I have had a flick through these provisions and my thoughts are as follows:

* Although the drafting of clauses 2.5-2.7 is quite odd in places, IMO these do not raise any ‘super red flags’ from a Privacy POV.
* My main concern is with the inclusion of Clause 17, which is effectively a series of data processing terms. I understand from the below that we will not be sharing or disclosing any personal data to the vendor - Clause 17 suggests otherwise at face value. As such, {color:#ff5630}*can you please double-check that we are 100% certain no personal data will be shared*{color} {color:#ff5630}*under this arrangement at any point* {color}(from Bolt to the vendor, and vice-versa)?
** If personal data _will_ be shared, then  I will need to do a much deeper dive of Clause 17 and suggest amendments, as it may not be fit for purpose.
** If personal data _will not_ be shared, can you please confirm with the vendor why Clause 17 has been included? 

Happy to discuss over a call, if easier 🙂

+*BACKGROUND*+

* Bolt has reached out to an accounting vendor in Romania to better understand tax implications for fleet / driver partners (i.e., the various possible legal setups our drivers and fleets can use, as well as the taxation implications for each). 
* It appears that the vendor has provided an agreement for Bolt to sign on 30 October. 
** Originally provided in Romanian. However, on 10 Dec, English version provided.
** Agreement is ‘Terms and Conditions for the provision of Tax Consultancy Services’.
*** Parties are both Romanian. Vendor is the Provider, Bolt is the Beneficiary.
*** Priced based on an hourly rate.
*** Contract is concluded for an ‘unlimited duration’.
*** Per clause 8.2, vendor’s aggregate liability is limited to the lower of (i) the fee received for the contested services and (ii) the amount insured by the civil liability policy taken out in this respect.
* On 10 December, Privacy were looped in as according to the agreement “_we are obliged to also share personal data with them_”. The ask is for us to review clauses 2.5, 2.6, 2.7 and 17, to bring out ‘super red flags’.

*2.5*

The provision of the services agreed upon by the Contract shall be limited taking into account that the services will be performed as an external service provider, which is not privy to all information and activities that are routinely carried out in the day-to-day business of the Beneficiary, and that the Beneficiary will provide the Provider or a third party with primary documents, supporting documents of the transactions carried out, in person at the Provider's premises or by electronic data transfer from a third party, and that the information will be discussed as a rule at the Provider's premises and by exception at another location. The Provider shall not be liable for the failure to record/not to process/not to process or not to report any documents or information relating to the Transactions of the Beneficiary, if they have not been made available to the Provider, or have been made available to the Provider late in relation to the standard deadline or the deadline agreed by the parties, for the documents and transactions that are necessary for the Provider to be able to fulfill its mission.

*2.6*

In view of the fact that the Beneficiary may also enter into other service contracts with another entity within the Group for other services, the Beneficiary expressly consents that all materials and where applicable data obtained as a result of the provision of the Services, including those containing personal data, shall be freely transferred to the Group solely for the purpose of fulfilling the obligations that any of the Group companies has undertaken to the Beneficiary. In this regard, the Beneficiary expressly consents to the free transfer of personal data by Provider within the Group

*2.7*

For the avoidance of doubt, the Provider shall have no legal or conventional obligation to retain and/or archive documents received from the Beneficiary, all documents and data being destroyed or archived where applicable and all personal data being deleted or archived by the Provider upon termination of the Contract within the time limits set out in this Contract and in accordance with the Provider's internal procedures or electronically archived internally or externally. The Service Provider shall not be liable to the Beneficiary for the failure to provide the documents destroyed upon termination of the Contract. All obligations to archive, preserve and make available any documents covered by the Contract to any public institutions or authorities shall be the sole responsibility of the Beneficiary. Also upon termination of the Contract, the Contractor may hand over the archives and all necessary information to the Beneficiary, under the conditions set out in the Contract. The archives, documents and information may be handed over only on the basis of a written acknowledgment of receipt or, as the case may be, by post or courier, and by this The Provider shall be released from liability.

*17*

The Parties shall comply with the rules and obligations imposed by the specific legislation in force on the protection of personal data and understand that the European rules of EU Regulation 679/2016 on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (GDPR) as well as the relevant domestic rules, apply to any data controller or processor located in the European Union and to any person processing personal data of data subjects located in the European Union or providing services to them;
Within the meaning of the GDPR, the Beneficiary (accounting services) is the Personal Data Processor and the Provider (accountant/chartered accountant, accountancy firm) is the Processor (or Authorized Person), who processes personal data on behalf of the Controller, in accordance with Art. 28 et seq. of the GDPR. Regulation;
[Additional provisions are effectively a DPA]

* The team since updated us that “_we will not be sharing or disclosing any personal information relating to any of our partners or employees, so it won’t be affecting us in any way_”.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* 2.5
** This does not raise any obvious Privacy concerns. Does not seem to directly relate to privacy issues.
* 2.6
** This does not raise any major red flags. It essentially says that the vendor can transfer data to other vendor group companies where those group companies also have obligations to the beneficiary. The use of the word ‘consent’ is odd, but not a dealbreaker.
** If personal data are involved, then we would need to ensure that appropriate data sharing / processing  sub-processing agreements are in place. However, it sounds like this is not the case.
* 2.7
** This provision is slightly odd, as the vendor cannot contract out of any legal obligations to retain data. 
** If no personal data are being processed, the the Provider not being liable for not providing docs after they have been destroyed is not necessarily a Privacy issue. However, we should confirm this, as if A28 GDPR applies then this would not be right.
* 17
** This provision does not make sense at all. If anything, Bolt would likely be the *_controller_* (not processor). In any case, we have been told no personal data sharing is going on here, so this needs to be bottomed out. 
** The A28 wording is also poorly drafted. I will do a deep dive of this if it is confirmed that a controller-processor relationship exists.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Check that Bolt is the beneficiary here.
* Double-check that no personal data is being shared under this agreement.
** If this is correct, then no super red flags from a Privacy POV for clauses 2.5-2.7. However, I would question why clause 17 is needed at all, as its inclusion is very misleading.
** If this is incorrect, then deeper analysis is needed. 
*** Depending on detailed nature of instructions (per EDPB guidance), vendor could be regarded as processor or controller. If a controller, then various parts of the agreement (particularly clause 17) need to be changed.
*** If vendor is a processor, then I need to do a deeper dive of clause 17. May suggest our own terms, since they are clearer. TBC.

“Dear Dear Dr. Mangala Kittur,

 

Thank you for the data subject request that you submitted on behalf of your client, which was received by us on *26 September 2024*.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to this access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals or their representatives to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies data subjects, or enables to be identified from it as a living individual person.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

In your request, you specifically asked for the invoices of the most three recent months that your client was working with our platform. Therefore, we are providing the following information regarding the personal data we hold about your client, to which you are entitled:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;

* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*The Data Subject’s rights*

The Data Subject has the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning him or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email. 

 

Yours sincerely,

Bolt”
